surprises.description: The preview expected a slight Q3 sales miss against its $1.85–$1.86 billion consensus bar; Hubbell instead reported $1.873 billion, a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net sales rose 25% year-over-year to $1.873 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect a modest revenue miss against a stretched $1.85B bar”; consensus was “$1.85B … / $1.86B.”

surprises.description: Electrical Solutions organic growth and profitability were well above the preview’s estimates: organic growth was 22% versus a 13–15% segment-build estimate, and its adjusted margin reached 24.8% versus an expected roughly 21.5–22%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “11% organic growth (22% in Electrical Solutions and 5% in Utility Solutions)” and Electrical Solutions adjusted operating margins “expanded 400 basis points year-over-year to 24.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment build estimated Electrical Solutions “Organic +13–15%”; the preview said its adjusted margin “must be >21.5%, ideally >22%” and its base case was “~21.5–22%.”

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted operating margin was 25.5%, substantially above the preview’s roughly 24.3% Q3 estimate, rather than merely delivering the needed second-half expansion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 adjusted operating margin at “~24.3%” and said “Q3 alone needs ~24.3%.”

surprises.description: Data center sales grew over 80% organically, far faster than the preview’s roughly 45–55% Q3 expectation; management also expects the business to reach about 15% of Electrical revenue by year-end and keep growing strongly in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center sales surged over 80% organically in the quarter” and are expected to represent “about 15% of Electrical segment revenues exiting 2026,” with “continued strong growth anticipated in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “data center +45–55%” and described the FY target as “~+50%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its sales outlook to 18–19% growth, above the prior 16–18% frame, with Electrical Solutions organic growth guidance raised to 17–18%. This is a stronger upgrade than the preview’s expected narrow-to-slightly-higher overall guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised “Electrical Solutions organic growth guidance to 17–18% and total sales growth to 18–19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY guidance of “+16–18%” and expected “a narrow-to-slightly-higher FY guide.”

surprises.description: Utility Solutions underperformed the preview’s growth expectation, and management cut its full-year organic growth outlook to 6–7% from the preview’s 7–9% target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Utility Solutions delivered “5%” organic growth, and management “lowered the Utility Solutions full-year organic growth outlook to 6-7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment build estimated Utility Solutions at “+10–11%”; it also cited a FY target of “+7–9% organic.”

surprises.description: A temporary meters component shortage shifted about $15 million of revenue out of Q3 and into Q4, an unanticipated near-term disruption to the Grid Automation line the preview expected to turn positive. Production was restored, with double-digit Grid Automation growth expected in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A temporary meters component shortage shifted approximately $15 million of revenue from Q3 into Q4, with full production already restored and double-digit Grid Automation growth expected in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Grid Automation to show Q3 growth of “+5% or better.”

surprises.description: NSI was not only contributing materially at accretive margins but was also integrating ahead of plan, easing the integration concern the preview identified as a key swing factor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The NSI acquisition contributed 29 points to Electrical Solutions revenue growth at accretive margins and is tracking ahead of initial integration expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called NSI “the swing factor on both growth and the leverage critique” and said “the NSI integration gets re-underwritten” if Electrical margins were weak.

surprises.description: Utility backlog had built by more than $500 million year-to-date, about 30% since the start of the year, providing stronger-than-typical visibility into 2027 and reinforcing the forward demand picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utility Solutions backlog built by over $500 million year-to-date (up roughly 30% since the start of the year), providing stronger-than-typical visibility into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited H1 book-to-bill of “~1.2x with orders booking into 2027” and flagged Utility book-to-bill and 2027 framing as key metrics.

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete 2027 outlook of at least mid-single-digit organic growth, 25–30% incrementals, and price-cost-productivity neutral to dollar-positive, providing more specific support for the 2027 setup than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “2027 organic growth of at least mid-single digits with price-cost-productivity neutral to dollar-positive and incrementals of 25-30%.”

surprises.description: Electrical price increases are being accelerated into Q4, a stronger near-term pricing action than the preview’s expectation that pricing would continue to hold against material costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “accelerating Electrical price increases into Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said pricing was “tracking 3–4 pts for FY26” and flagged whether price was “still fully covering material cost.”

surprises.description: Quarterly capacity additions are expected to double from about $25 million in 2026 to $50 million in 2027, concentrated in transmission, substation, and data center markets. This adds a significant capacity ramp that the preview did not specify, with growth potential balanced against its concerns about spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly incremental capacity additions were about $25 million per quarter in 2026 and are expected to roughly double to $50 million per quarter in 2027, concentrated in transmission, substation, and data center markets.”

surprises.description: The raised full-year adjusted EPS range of $20.40–$20.60 was broadly near the preview’s base-case range, but fell short of its highlighted $20.70-or-higher raise scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $20.40-$20.60, representing 12-13% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “$20.45–$20.65,” while its catalyst checklist highlighted “raise to ≥$20.70 vs. mere narrowing.”
